title: Benchmark telemetry warehouse, comparison UI, and anomaly triage workflow
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a robust persistent store and comparison UI for automated benchmark runs (tokens/sec, p95, p99, failure rate, GPU mem/SM utilization) plus an operational triage workflow that surfaces regressions and guides on-call and SREs through validation and rollback. This ticket covers schema design, ingestion pipeline, comparison APIs, a lightweight web UI in Console, and the scripted triage checklist and alerting integration.

Why: Current benchmark runs are ad-hoc and ephemeral. We lack a normalized way to compare runs across model variants, quantization, kernel selections, and hardware. That makes regressions invisible until a customer incident. Persisting runs with rich metadata enables regression detection, historical baselines, and automated anomaly triage.

High-level approach:
- Store canonical run objects in a high-throughput columnar store (ClickHouse) for fast aggregate queries across millions of tokens and thousands of runs.
- Normalize payload to: run_id, timestamp, env (host/region), model_id, model_version, quantization_profile, kernel_set, hw_type (A100/V100/Grav), batch_size, seq_distribution_summary, workload_id, workload_seed, tokens_processed, tokens_per_sec, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, failure_count, gpu_mem_mb, gpu_util_pct, kv_hit_rate.
- Ingestion: batched uploader (go service) that writes compressed parquet->ClickHouse; dedupe on run_id and validate schema. Backfill tool for legacy CSV exports.
- Comparison API: endpoints to fetch single-run, side-by-side diff, and aggregated baseline over selected time window; support percentile-aligned comparisons (e.g., compare p95 for 1024 seqs).
- Anomaly detection: baseline selection (rolling median of N runs or tagged stable run), compute relative delta and z-score; apply hysteresis thresholds and significance tests (bootstrap for non-normal distributions). Configurable thresholds by metric and workload.
- Triage flow: automated alert creation (Slack + Console alerts) with auto-populated triage checklist, related infra metrics links (Grafana), recent PRs that touched runtime or kernels (GitHub link), and a one-click replay runner to re-run the benchmark on the same hardware if available. Alerts escalate to SRE/owner when customer_impact=high or sustained regression > 3 hours.

Out of scope for this ticket: auto-rollback plumbing for model routing, long-term ML-model quality checks (separate PM ticket), and full RBAC for benchmark access (follow-up).

Success criteria / acceptance criteria:
- Persistent storage accepts and indexes 10k runs/day with average write latency < 2s per batch ingest.
- Console UI displays run comparison (two run side-by-side + baseline summary) with token/sec and p95 graphs and heatmap of sequence-length buckets.
- Automated detector flags regressions with reproducible alert messages; first-run detection precision > 85% while keeping false positive rate under 10% in the test window.
- Triage checklist shows correlated infra metrics and links to the most-likely culprit PRs.

Security & privacy notes: run payloads may contain prompt fingerprints — strip PII and only store workload_id and hash of prompts. Security review required for retention policy and access controls.

qa_test_plan: 1) Unit tests for schema validation and dedupe behavior. 2) End-to-end ingest test (CLI -> S3 -> ClickHouse) using synthetic runs. 3) Detector A/B: run dataset with injected regressions and measure precision/recall. 4) UI acceptance: run comparison rendering across heavy and light workloads. 5) Security checks: verify prompt hashing, KMS encryption, and retention enforcement in dev. 6) Load test: simulate 10k runs/day and measure ingest latency and ClickHouse query p95.
implementation_notes: - Ingest service (go): parallel worker pool, per-run gzip compression, validation against JSON schema. - ClickHouse tables: runs_raw (mergeTree by run_id), runs_aggregated (materialized views for daily_baselines), run_metrics (per-bucket time-series for seq buckets). - API endpoints: /bench/runs/{id}, /bench/compare?left={id}&right={id}&baseline_window=30d, /bench/alerts. - UI: React component in Console->Performance with Plotly for percentile lines and custom heatmap for seq distribution. - Alerting: use Alertmanager hook to populate slack channel #bench-alerts and create Console incident with triage template.
risks: 1) ClickHouse hosting cost and query contention if materialized views not tuned. 2) False positives creating alert fatigue. 3) Ingest skew: very large runs causing long copy times. 4) Sensitive prompt contents inadvertently stored.
mitigations: 1) Add TTL and rollup policies; evaluate cost after 4 weeks of ingest. 2) Use bootstrap confidence and require correlated infra signals before auto-escalation. 3) Enforce per-run size cap and chunk large runs at ingest. 4) Enforce prompt hashing and schema validation; security review for retention policy.
